result.summary: The street provides continuous sidewalks on both sides with mature trees and street lighting, creating a generally walkable environment. However, the lack of marked crosswalks at the visible intersection and sightline obstructions from parked cars reduce overall pedestrian safety.

result.summary: The image depicts a mid-block urban residential street with a continuous, paved sidewalk in good condition. Pedestrians are separated from the roadway by a curb and a line of parallel-parked cars, which provide a physical barrier but also obstruct sightlines. The environment lacks street trees, lighting, and active ground-floor frontages, resulting in a functional but sterile pedestrian experience.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line between the sidewalk and the street

hazards.name: Lack of Active Frontage
hazards.description: The long, windowless grey wall at street level reduces natural surveillance and engagement with the public realm.

interventions.description: Installing street trees or planters would provide a physical buffer from traffic and improve the aesthetic quality of the walkway.
